subject: sampler bug on Windows vs. Mac

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: sampler bug on Windows vs. Mac
parts:
I can reproduce the odd behavior on my Mac with the
current master from GitHub.

This model works fine:

parameters {
real theta;
}
model {
theta ~ normal(0,1);
}

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
theta 0.0 0.0 1.0 -1.9 -0.5 0.0 0.6 1.9 699 1.0


But this one fails:

parameters {
real theta;
}
model {
0 ~ normal(theta,1);
}

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
theta -0.3 0.1 0.6 -1.3 -0.9 -0.3 0.1 0.6 24 1.0


Yet this one succeeds:

parameters {
real theta;
}
model {
0.0 ~ normal(theta,1);
}

mean se_mean sd 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% n_eff Rhat
theta 0.0 0.0 0.9 -1.8 -0.5 -0.0 0.5 1.9 607 1.0


So I'm thinking it's probably an issue with how int
vs. double is being treated somewhere in the modeling
language. The only difference is in the following log_prob
function line:

lp__ += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(0.0, theta, 1);

Not clear how this could be causing problems, because the following
unit test (not committed/pushed) passes:

TEST(ProbDistributionsNormal, intVsDouble) {
using stan::agrad::var;
var theta(1.9);
var lp1(0.0);
lp1 += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(0, theta, 1);
double lp1val = lp1.val();
lp1.grad();
double lp1adj = lp1.adj();

var theta2(1.9);
var lp2(0.0);
lp2 += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(0.0, theta2, 1);
double lp2val = lp2.val();
lp2.grad();
double lp2adj = lp2.adj();
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(lp1val,lp2val);
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(lp1adj,lp2adj);
}

I'm not going to actively work on this right now, but
thought I'd share this much.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sampler bug on Windows vs. Mac
parts:
Beat me to an email by a few minutes. I've been wrestling with this all night (gotta go to bed now if I want to wake up early for the first day at UCL) and all I can conclude is that the effect is very, very small but not random and so accumulates over very long warm-up periods. It's not immediately clear if it's due to the sampler or the adaptation, but it's hard to see any effect on a single leapfrog step. Small differences in log_prog or grad_log_prob could be the culprit.

Bob, I would actually expect those tests to pass given the size of the effect. EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ has a pretty high threshold, much larger than the effect I'm seeing (which is dangerously close to the floating point precision limit). Shouldn't those values be derived from the same calculations and hence be exactly equal?
